title: A novel comparison of live whale body condition assessment methods from lateral images with necropsy-derived metrics and histology in gray whales (Eschrichtius robustus)
content:
Abstract
Body condition (BC) is a critical indicator of health, reproductive viability and ecosystem capacity in cetaceans. Validating BC assessment methods from live animals against direct physiological measurements remains challenging, particularly in large whales. BC of live grey whales (Eschrichtius robustus) is commonly assessed from lateral imagery by categorical scoring systems, although these have not been directly compared to necropsy-derived metrics. We evaluated two live whale lateral BC assessment methods, the Bradford scoring system and the recently developed angle of BC (°BC), using photographs of live grey whales in San Francisco Bay that were subsequently matched to stranded carcasses. Inter-rater reliability was high for both methods, and results were correlated as expected. We then compared each live BC assessment method to necropsy-derived metrics including blubber depth, qualitative blubber characteristics, state of nutrition (SON) and adipocyte histology at three blubber levels: deep, middle and superficial. Neither °BC nor Bradford score was significantly associated with blubber thickness or characteristics, suggesting that blubber depth is an unreliable proxy for nutritional condition. Notably, °BC significantly predicted SON while Bradford scores showed weaker and non-significant relationships with SON. Adipocytes in the deep blubber layer were depleted and therefore not assessable. Furthermore, °BC significantly predicted adipocyte morphology of the middle blubber layer but not the superficial layer, and the deep layer was too depleted for assessment. Contrastingly, Bradford scores did not predict adipocyte morphology at any layer. These findings provide the first direct comparison of live large whale BC assessment against necropsy-derived metrics in the same individuals, supporting the use of quantitative lateral-image analysis as a sensitive non-invasive tool for assessing grey whale health. Additionally, the significance of °BC as a predictor of adipocyte morphology indicates that nutritional status can be reasonably inferred from blubber histology with limited imagery or samples available.
